forward_risk_review.surface: Restore lifecycle cleanup and later rollback
forward_risk_review.reason: A successful forward restore cleanup must persist a terminal authority that can be reconciled or reused if a later deployment phase fails.

forward_risk_review.surface: Fresh-install automatic rollback and evidence separation
forward_risk_review.reason: The accepted hotfix must produce a strict seven-field application rollback plus independent cleanup authority and remove only the frozen production and restore resources.
checks: run the real PostgreSQL 17.10 Docker acceptance at the exact head
verify aggregate and terminal digests remain separate from the application rollback projection
inspect partial cleanup, late orphan, same-name replacement and application failure tests

decision.rationale: The exact-head checks and fresh-install Docker acceptance pass, but the normal forward restore cleanup returns PASS after moving the V2 lifecycle to QUIESCING and deleting resources without persisting CLEANED or a cleanup reference. A later phase failure therefore cannot reconcile that cleanup and can turn an otherwise safe rollback into ROLLBACK_FAILED.

summary: PR #8 correctly binds the configured database principal, adds exact attempt labels, performs identity-safe fresh-install cleanup and passes its real Docker rollback acceptance. One blocking lifecycle integration defect remains: the normal RESTORE phase leaves successful cleanup authority in QUIESCING, so later rollback/replay is not valid.

findings.title: Forward restore cleanup never completes its V2 lifecycle
findings.observation: The normal RESTORE phase calls cleanupIsolatedRestoreEnvironment, which only forwards cleanupOwnedProject. That helper freezes the lifecycle in QUIESCING, deletes the resources and returns PASS. The only code that persists rollback-cleanup.json and calls completeLifecycle is executeRollbackWithCleanup, which this forward path never invokes. The prior tests that asserted forward cleanup persisted CLEANED were removed, and the replacement tests inspect only the returned CleanupResult.
findings.trigger: Run the normal RESTORE phase to a successful cleanup, or call cleanupIsolatedRestoreEnvironment after a READY RestoreLifecycleV2, then inspect restore-lifecycle.json. If a subsequent PRODUCTION_UNCHANGED or POST_RESTORE_SMOKE phase fails, automatic rollback re-enters cleanup with an empty live set and the previously frozen non-empty ownedBeforeCleanup set.
findings.impact: The durable lifecycle remains QUIESCING with no cleanup reference even though all restore resources were deleted. A later rollback cannot reconcile the successful cleanup, produces a cleanup set mismatch and can terminate ROLLBACK_FAILED instead of completing the otherwise safe fresh-install rollback. This contradicts the required CLEANED terminal authority and replay behavior.

evidence.description: A review-only exact-head test created a READY restore lifecycle, ran cleanupOwnedProject to PASS, then read restore-lifecycle.json. The assertion expected CLEANED but received QUIESCING.
The forward wrapper returns cleanupOwnedProject directly and the RESTORE phase accepts its PASS without completing a lifecycle.
cleanupOwnedProject persists QUIESCING before deletion and returns PASS; completeLifecycle is called only from executeRollbackWithCleanup after aggregate evidence persistence.
The approved V2 lifecycle requires successful cleanup to transition QUIESCING to CLEANED with a PASS cleanup reference, and replay must reconcile byte-valid terminal authority.

findings.remediation: Give the normal forward restore cleanup a complete immutable authority path: persist a compatible cleanup record/reference and transition the exact QUIESCING lifecycle to CLEANED before returning PASS. Re-entry after successful deletion must resolve the terminal reference and confirm the live project remains empty instead of comparing the empty set with the old frozen set.
findings.verification: Add a regression that executes the forward restore cleanup, requires restore-lifecycle.json state CLEANED with a resolvable PASS reference, then injects a later phase failure/recovery and proves the same exact cleanup reconciles without ROLLBACK_FAILED or additional deletion.

required_actions.action: Complete and persist the forward restore cleanup lifecycle, then cover later rollback/replay after that cleanup.

risks.description: A post-restore deployment failure can encounter a non-terminal lifecycle whose resources were already deleted.
risks.mitigation: Block merge until PRR-001 adds terminal cleanup authority and a later-failure regression.

risks.description: No production deployment, DNS, public endpoint, real secret or production database was exercised in Review.
risks.mitigation: Keep production execution behind the separate release authorization and acceptance workflow.
